## Impact and Engagement

- **UK Infected Blood Inquiry** (2022). With the Scottish National Blood Transfusion Service (NHS), I studied survival after blood transfusion and how age at first transfusion, sex and the number of red-cell units received affect it. The work was carried out at the request of the Inquiry. [\[Report\]](https://www.infectedbloodinquiry.org.uk/sites/default/files/documents/WITN7586003%20-%20%2522%20Scotland%27s%20covariate-adjusted%20survival%20to%2031December%202019%20for%201999-cohort%20and%202004-cohort%2522%2C%20%2008%20December%202022%20.pdf) [\[Scottish Government response\]](https://www.gov.scot/publications/first-minister-responds-uk-infected-blood-inquiry-final-report/) [\[BBC coverage\]](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crgg2nx31j0o)
- **ASA DataFest at the University of Edinburgh** (2024--2026). Co-organiser of the American Statistical Association's data-analysis hackathon for students. Our experience is described in Sharifi Far et al. (2026), *Teaching Statistics*. [\[Paper\]](https://doi.org/10.1111/test.12404) [\[2026 website\]](https://edi-datafest26.netlify.app/)
- **Taster lecture** for prospective undergraduates: *Can We Trust a Positive Test? A Statistical Perspective on Medical Diagnosis* (2026). [\[Slides\]](files/slides_taster_lecture.pdf)
